reports.summary: **Test Results #71** - The idle state is displayed correctly with the enlarged Record button when no takes are available. - The take list is displayed correctly after recording, showing the take number, waveform, duration, play/pause button, selection indicator, and delete icon. - Users can play, pause, and select a take successfully, and only one take can be selected at a time. - Recording a new take works correctly. The take list collapses during recording, and the new take is added to the bottom of the list and selected automatically after recording stops. - The Record New Take button is disabled after reaching the maximum limit of five takes, preventing additional recordings. - Deleting takes works correctly. Non-selected takes are deleted immediately, selected takes show a confirmation prompt, and the app returns to the idle state when the last take is deleted. **Issue Identified:** The recording timer overlaps the audio waveform after a take is recorded. Move the timer above the waveform to the right side.

reports.author: JonathanSeehagen
reports.summary:
**Finding from the #528 audit (Play, record, and re-record audio)**

Device: Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 10, running merged `main` against `dev.api.fluent.bible`.

In verse mode, tapping the middle of a draft take's waveform now **seeks to the tapped position**, but:

- playback **starts on its own** after the tap, and
- the take control keeps showing **Play** instead of Pause.

In `useVerseAudio.seek`, `playingTakeId` is set but no `PLAY` is dispatched, so the card's `isThisPlaying` (which requires `state === 'playing'`) stays false.

The same tap also raises `Maximum update depth exceeded` (dev LogBox). That is tracked separately in #569.

Suggested additional AC for this issue:

- [ ] After a waveform tap, the take control reflects the real playback state (Pause while playing), and playback does not auto-start unless it was already playing.

Assessment: `docs/assessments/play-record-rerecord-audio/` (PR #566).

Reproduced during the offline chapter assignment audit (#533) with a single chapter.

**Confirmed on:** Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 10 (API 29), local debug build of `main` @ `fb634e5` (without PR #559), `dev.api.fluent.bible` (2026-09-28 16:57, Acts 6).

- One offline take on one chapter; turning Wi-Fi on started **two** automatic upload sessions 2 ms apart (16:57:41.638 and .640), with notification start/clear pairs within 2 ms.
- The app then crashed with `RemoteServiceException: Context.startForegroundService() did not then call Service.startForeground()` (`UploadSyncForegroundService`) at 16:57:43.
- Duplicate sessions per trigger were seen again on 2026-09-29 (Sync Now at 08:03 started three sessions; the reconnect at 12:02 started two).

So the crash does not need many chapters; a duplicate session on one reconnect is enough.

Assessment: `docs/assessments/offline-chapter-assignment/README.md` (PR #609).

## Returning online and synchronizing changes audit — tests executed

These are the tests run to reach the results and gaps in this audit.

All tests were run on a physical Android device with access to Wi-Fi and mobile data.

### A. Baseline

- **A.1** Online on Wi-Fi, nothing pending. Expected: header green `cloud-check`; Sync page "Upload complete" / "All synced", no controls.
- **A.2** Airplane mode, nothing pending. Expected: header gray `cloud-check`.

### B. Coming back online with takes recorded offline

- **B.4** Still offline, open the Sync page. Expected: offline copy; Sync Now not actionable, with a reason.
- **B.5** Back on Home, turn airplane mode off (Wi-Fi only, toggle off) and do nothing. Expected: upload starts on its own, no prompt; header shows syncing.
- **B.6** Open the Sync page during the upload. Expected: animated icon; "Uploading"; "X of Y chapters uploaded" with Y = chapters, never going backwards; Pause + Cancel.

reports.author: JonathanSeehagen
reports.summary:
The offline chapter assignment audit (#533) covered this issue's behavior on device (`main` @ `fb634e5`, Android 10, `dev.api.fluent.bible`).

- **Pass:** translator-vs-translator race pushed within 5 minutes, no peer checker (D.3–D.7): the claim returns a conflict, the conflict indicator shows on both devices, the Record banner appears, and it persists across syncs.
- **Fail:** a PM assignment (web sets a peer checker) or an offline window longer than 5 minutes: the claim gets 404 on every sync, no conflict is shown, and the take is stranded → #610.
- **Fail:** pending claims are pushed only by the full sync, so the reconnect upload and the list refresh act before them → #611.
- PM conflict resolution was not tested (out of scope here, per this issue).

Assessment: `docs/assessments/offline-chapter-assignment/README.md` (PR #609).

reports.author: JonathanSeehagen
reports.summary:
## Returning online and synchronizing changes audit — tests executed

These are the tests run to reach the results and gaps in this audit.

All tests were run on a physical Android device with access to Wi-Fi and mobile data.

### A. Baseline

- **A.1** Online on Wi-Fi, nothing pending. Expected: header green `cloud-check`; Sync page "Upload complete" / "All synced", no controls.
- **A.2** Airplane mode, nothing pending. Expected: header gray `cloud-check`.

### B. Coming back online with takes recorded offline

- **B.3** In airplane mode, record takes in 2+ chapters, several verses each. Expected: header gray pending variant; chapter rows show pending.
- **B.4** Still offline, open the Sync page. Expected: offline copy; Sync Now not actionable, with a reason.
- **B.5** Back on Home, turn airplane mode off (Wi-Fi only, toggle off) and do nothing. Expected: upload starts on its own, no prompt; header shows syncing.
- **B.6** Open the Sync page during the upload. Expected: animated icon; "Uploading"; "X of Y chapters uploaded" with Y = chapters, never going backwards; Pause + Cancel.

reports.author: JonathanSeehagen
reports.summary:
Reproduced during the offline chapter assignment audit (#533) with a single chapter.

**Confirmed on:** Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 10 (API 29), local debug build of `main` @ `fb634e5` (without PR #559), `dev.api.fluent.bible` (2026-09-28 16:57, Acts 6).

- One offline take on one chapter; turning Wi-Fi on started **two** automatic upload sessions 2 ms apart (16:57:41.638 and .640), with notification start/clear pairs within 2 ms.
- The app then crashed with `RemoteServiceException: Context.startForegroundService() did not then call Service.startForeground()` (`UploadSyncForegroundService`) at 16:57:43.
- Duplicate sessions per trigger were seen again on 2026-09-29 (Sync Now at 08:03 started three sessions; the reconnect at 12:02 started two).

So the crash does not need many chapters; a duplicate session on one reconnect is enough.

Assessment: `docs/assessments/offline-chapter-assignment/README.md` (PR #609).
